Text: My original purchase actually never got sent to me/was missing from my package, but, customer service easily resolved this and "replaced" the item, so, once I finally got what I paid for, I was quite satisfied with what I'd purchased!  I bought this with the intention to use it to charge my SteamDeck, which requires a dedicated 15V at 3 Amps to charge (especially if you're playing it while charging).  Cons first: this little thing is a brick -- it's heavy, it's dense, but! It's decently compact! And foldable, which makes it wonderful for travel! I originally wanted something that could power multiple devices if it was going to be chunky, but, unfortunately, I was unable to find a charging block with multiple ports with the dedicated power that I needed. Most of what I found might have claimed to be 3A+, but, when you look at the output power for 15V, that usually dropped down to 1-2A, which, won't charge the SteamDeck as desired. So, I settled on this charging block.  Now, for the Pros: It's definitely less bulky than the SteamDeck's original charger, and, I can buy whatever length cord or cord style that I want! It feels like it's a really solidly built charging block, but, more importantly, it gives me the proper power that I needed to charge my SteamDeck. For smart devices (such as the Samsung Tablet S7), it can easily super/fast charge them too! Despite it being a little heavy and a mini-chunk, it's a mighty little thing, does what it needs to, and is of good quality. Very satisfied with this purchase!

I've been using Anker's 65W GaN chargers for years now, and this is actually a replacement after my toddler decided to give my previous one an unexpected water bath! That should tell you something about how much I trust this charger - when I needed a replacement, I didn't even consider other options.  **What I Love:** This thing is my catch-all charging solution. I regularly use it to power my Samsung Galaxy S23, Lenovo ThinkPad T480, and Galaxy Tab S6 Lite, and it handles all three without breaking a sweat. The 65W output is perfect for this range of devices - plenty of power for my laptop while not being overkill for my phone.  The compact size is honestly the standout feature for me. For a charger that can handle everything from phones to laptops, it's remarkably small and travel-friendly. I can toss it in any bag without thinking twice about space or weight.  **Performance:** Charging speeds are consistently good across all my devices. My ThinkPad charges at full speed, my phone gets rapid charging, and the tablet powers up quickly too. I've never had any scenarios where it underperformed or couldn't handle what I threw at it.  **Build Quality:** Rock solid construction. My previous one lasted years of daily use and travel before meeting its watery end (definitely not the charger's fault!). The fact that I immediately bought the exact same model as a replacement speaks to how reliable these are.  **Bottom Line:** If you need one charger that can handle multiple devices reliably, this is it. Compact, powerful, and built to last. Highly recommended for anyone looking to simplify their charging setup.

So, the fantastic thing about PowerA controllers is that they're dirt cheap, esp compared to your wireless microsoft ones. The downside? They wont last you more than a few weeks before you start getting issues with the joysticks, triggers, or buttons(I'd bought four in the past for split-screen, which I have swapped out using as they have failed). My last PowerA controller was actually fairly old, but finally had developed a mushy B-button which I knew I couldn't fix, so I ordered a new one which arrived about a week ago. Now I've been using it fairly regularly since then, but it has ALREADY developed a ghost input on the left trigger that causes it to act like the trigger is being held down around 5-10%. Now, the reason I clarified that my previous PowerA controller was fairly old is because USUALLY the ghost inputs or joystick drifts can be solved by opening up the controller, dabbing some rubbing alcohol on the sensor, running it through its motion a few times, and then giving it a few minutes to dry. When I bought this one, I was really hoping PowerA would have achieved a bit more reliability in the few years since I last bought a controller from them, but it looks like it'll probably be the same old song and dance with this one as well. Fortunately I'm used to it, but if you want to avoid the struggle, just pay the extra money for a proper controller that will last.  And for those that already have one and are experiencing issues, remember: pop it open, dab on some rubbing alcohol(make sure it's 91% to avoid as much water contamination as possible, and be sure it's really immersed to wash off the contact surfaces inside), run it through its range of motion, and keep your fingers crossed. That usually does it, but if that doesn't fix the problem then just buy a better controller next time...

After reading all the great reviews on this controller I decided to give it a try especially with it being much lower in price. What I got is what I paid for.  When the controller first came in it was extremely light but felt good holding it. For any person buying this I HIGHLY recommend you turn off the vibration. (I feel like the vibration likely caused some of its faults as time went). After using the controller for about two weeks I noticed a tiny shadow drift effect that I wasn’t sure if it was my internet or the controller. After week three the controller definitely had a bad drift in all directions. After week four the controller started having issues where the analog clicks stopped working and also the triggers start randomly freaking out glitching. After week five the controller started randomly having a mind of its own turning on my xbox and loving into games while no one is home.(friends told me I was online when I wasn’t) I’ve watched this happen too.  So again the good reviews are deceiving and it’s what you pay for buying a cheap controller.

This is supposed to mimic an Xbox 360 controller. You would expect to be able to use the joysticks in 360 degrees. This is incorrect. I held the left stick up and jiggled it slightly left and right. My character continued to move directly forward. I pulled out a weapon I need to aim with the left stick. Moving the stick slightly did nothing. Moving it harder caused me to whip around like crazy. There is no "slightly" moving the control stick. It's either hard or nothing. It seems the control stick only reads 8 directions. Up, Up/Right, Right, etc. There is no in between. This makes it IMPOSSIBLE to aim any kind of weapon in first person.  Let's talk about the feel. The controller is hard plastic. It doesn't have any weight to it. It's extremely plastic. Go grab your actual Xbox 360 controller. Now take away 50% of the weight and make it a much harder plastic. The controller, with it's Micro-USB cable in the box feel just as a heavy as a normal 360 controller. YES THIS IS NOT A USB-C controller. Why is this controller not USB-C?? The left joystick has a lot of small bumps on it. I played with this for a good 20 minutes before quitting. Now 20 minutes after stopping playing my thumb still hurts.  Ultimately you get what you pay for with this. If you just want a decent controller it's fine. If you want to be able to precisely aim with a joystick go with something else.

I used this smartwatch for 2 months before writing this review. I'm a mountain biker and I've been using heart rate monitors for years, mostly the Polar line of watches and chest straps. A few years back I decided to try the first Fitbit Versa, as I wanted to see if a smartwatch could work as a good heart rate monitor during workouts as well. That Versa didn't work, the heart rate was inaccurate and all over the place, so I just kept using my Polar accessories, until this new Fitbit Versa 3 came along. I have tried this Fitbit Versa 3 on rides outdoors and on Spinning sessions indoors, and this is what I've experienced: - Outdoor rides: the GPS works almost flawlessly, the signal gets lost in the woods and around large buildings and large hills, but it comes back to normal quickly. The interface is gorgeous, clean, clear, easy to read, easy to handle during rides, fantastic in general but there's just one big problem, no matter how beautiful and easy to use is this, the heart rate monitor doesn't work. I ride on the same hilly areas all the time, I know how my heart rate behaves in certain hills and roads, up certain steep hills it gets all the way up to 200 bpm, but this watch NEVER once showed that number, it gets to 175 bpm and then it goes blank, the reader cannot handle a faster heart rate, it just goes crazy and stops working, then as I'm climbing the end of the hill it shows a 120 bpm number, which is the heart rate I get when I'm casually walking. Completely inaccurate and all over the place. The maximum heart rate this watch has read during my rides in 2 months is 176 bpm after an uphill that usually makes my heart go up to 200 bpm. After many times of bad readings, I tried both my Polar Ignite and this Versa 3 at the same time during my rides, and the difference was outstanding, the Polar (without a chest strap) was giving me all the right readings flawlessly while the Versa 3 was blank or inaccurate or all over place. All the same problems happened during my running and hiking workouts. - Spinning sessions: during Spinning sessions my heart goes up to 196/ 200 bpm, the Fitbit Versa again got stuck at 170/ 175 bpm and then went blank, and it was giving me bad readings the whole session, always below my actual heart rate, therefore messing up my stats and saying that I burnt a LOT less calories than I actually do. In the photo I'm attaching the Polar Ignite (left) shows my real heart rate and calories burnt during a workout, while the Versa 3 (right) shows the wrong heart rate and the wrong calories burnt, if you see the numbers, they are completely different. I've used this watch for 2 months and tried everything to make it work, all troubleshooting options , but nothing made the heart rate reader work properly. If you take your workouts and stats half-serious, this is not the watch for you, it works fine during casual workouts, like walking or gardening or doing light exercises that won't take your heart over the 180 bpm threshold, once you are higher that that the Versa 3 goes berserk, it cannot read anything faster than that. I'm sticking with my chunky, not-too-cool Polar watches, they may not look as beautiful as the Fitbit products, but they are hard working and completely accurate when it comes to tracking my heart rate, workouts and sports. After wearing this Fitbit Versa 3 smartwatch for 2 months: - The good: AMAZING battery life, about a week or so depending on your settings, beautiful interface, not many apps to use but enough for my usage, as I prefer to use my cellphone for apps in general, light and comfortable to wear, the new strap is cool and comfy, good to track steps, stairs and regular day long activity.Good and accurate GPS without the need for a cellphone. I never used the Alexa option so I cannot comment on that. I tried to respond to my text messages with the voice/dictation option (the watch has a microphone) and didn't work, it may be because I have an accent, who knows, but I think that option is pretty cool. FANTASTIC cellphone app to handle all your info and data. - The bad: AWFUL as a heart rate monitor, awful at sleep tracking, according to this watch I'm a zombie who sleeps 2 hours and has no heartbeat the rest of the night, some nights it won't even track one minute. Yes, I've tried wearing it higher or lower on my wrists, the left one and the right one, none of that made a difference. I hope that at some point Fitbit gets the right technology to make the heart rate reading sensors accurate (like other brands have already done), that'd make it an almost perfect smart watch and real activity tracker. I wish them the best, they are doing a great work with most of their products and one can see the effort and love they put on the things they create, except the damn heart rate sensors! ;)

I’m actually missing my Apple Watch, which I thought I was done with.

I used Fitbit for almost a year, the battery is AMAZING. You can go like 4-5 days without charging it. The reason I only gave 3 stars is because if you’re an athlete or avid exerciser... you probably would want to buy an Apple watch instead and just suffer through charging it every night lol. I say this because when comparing Fitbit and Apple during runs or any other workout, Apple is much more accurate on reading your heart rate. Fitbit does read your HR accurately but it takes like 5minutes to check up to why your HR actually is where Apple is in real time. This makes a huge difference if you’re training for something orrrr if you’re frustrated on your calorie burn during a workout. I burn way more calories during my workouts according to Apple Watch compared to Fitbit. This is because my HR is actually much higher during the workout than Fitbit thinks it is! If Fitbit could fix that, I would definitely switch back.

My wants were pretty basic. Needed to count steps. Thats it. I hike for exercise so what else would I need? The Versa did that well as long as I was synced with my phone. Then I started going to barre exercise classes. Used it to track calories burned. I also used and liked the watch, the heart rate, weather, timer, alexa (sometimes), I could turn off phone calls, etc features. I liked my watch! Then after 17 months the watch died. Boom. It was quick! Worked one day - died the next. Well, ya can't replace the battery. So I paid $200 for a watch that lasted not even a year and a half. My sister bought 2 and both died the same way. So unless you are OK with buying a new watch every 1.5 years I'd say don't do it. Get an Apple Watch or any other good fitness watch that includes a replaceable battery.

I've had this watch for about 2 years and about a week ago, the screen went completely black and unresponsive. I've tried factory resetting it and deleting it and re-pairing it to my phone and nothing. It's done beautifully this whole time. My review is more like a question to amazing if it's still within a warranty window?

I've had this watch for about 2 days now and I've been enjoying it. I have to admit the app can be some what counterintuitive to use but once you learn it, there's a lot of great info on it. HR monitoring isn't going to be spectacular and it doesn't pick up on the spikes very well when exercising but for everyday use, it should work well. Battery life , I've had to charge it once already so we'll see what happens with it. I'm really enjoying the sleeping data and find it pretty accurate. I've been looking at smart watches to help track my health/ exercise, sleep and to vibrate on my wrist as an alarm ( I work nights sometimes so I wanted to be able to wear war plugs without worrying about missing my alarm). I haven't had a problem with the button like some people have and have just been enjoying it.

Most of us already know, quite a bit about Fitbit, and there are reviews a plenty. What I want to talk about is the fact that Google purchased Fitbit and is now getting rid of all challenges as of March 27! As this is one of the biggest reasons I got Fitbit and not a much less expensive tracker, I think it is very important to know. Challenges are what set Fitbit apart. I don’t see any reason to continue purchasing Fitbit after this blatant disregard for customer wishes. In fact, it makes me question ever purchasing a Google product in the future, if their regard for their customers is so low

From time to time the watch will be behind 5 mins. or so. It will catch up. Right now I just noticed it’s 20 mins. behind. I have had it exactly a month. I hope it’s not too late to return it. My last Fitbit lasted for 5 years without any problems at all. Then it just died. But that was fine, I felt I had gotten my monies worth!!!

My device has been incredibly inaccurate counting stairs, counting as many as 40 flights on a day I did not have any, and will give me counts for flights of stairs walking 20 feet down a hallway at my office. I spoke to support who said it is a know issue "with no solution any time in the immediate future" (it has been a known issue for 6+ months) for this device and they WILL NOT replace the device because they will only replace with a same model and this is an issue with this model. They will only offer an alternative after their tech team says there is no solution able to be made (this has been a know issue for 6 months) and that hasn't been long enough. So if you buy it and have a similar issue your SOL.

This is my third Fitbit. It has been the most accurate compared to earlier versions of Charge ( replaced under warranty after 1 year then lasted 2 years) and Ionic lasted 2 years & glitchy). However less reliable on text & call notifications even with phone on my chest. I do not use the music feature or other apps accept the alarm, timer, stopwatch & exercise. My biggest complaint is the button is flat making it difficult to use with the arthritis in my hand & on all the time drains battery fast. Charger connects magnetically easy just wish it came with a longer one. Synchs nicely with my food app. Just be aware each of my Fitbit’s only lasted 2 years ( each September 🤷‍♀️).

I bought this primarily to track my mileage on runs as I'm training for a half marathon, and I'm fairly disappointed by this tracker in that regard. The Fitbit consistently logs less mileage on my runs than I'm actually doing - sometimes I lose as much as a mile on my tracker. For that reason, the data on my page, cadence, etc, is completely off. I've checked their forums and this is apparently a known issue. My $50 Samsung Galaxy Fit 2 is bang on in its tracking. It makes no sense!  I do think its sleep tracking tool is neat, and I was excited about the ability to export my run data as a spreadsheet, but again - that feature is completely useless if it's not logging the correct data. Save your money and buy a different watch.

A couple of years ago I wanted a smart watch that I could use for calls and emails. I went with the Samsung Galaxy Watch instead of a Fitbit, but I kept hoping FitBit would add these features, because I found the Fitbit fitness tracking and display to be superior. I thought the Versa 3 was it. Sadly, it is not.  I am returning for a few reasons. 1. The font is small, with no way to adjust it, except for on the watch face, 2. You can answer incoming calls, but not initiate calls. 3. You can view and respond to texts immediately, but there is no way to do so after a few seconds, and there is no way to initiate a text or even view past texts. Thus it is really more of a glorified tracker than a true smart watch.

Just buy the basic fitbit. I use mine daily to tract heart rate and calorie use. It tracks my sleep accurately. It documents similar to my sleep machine. Heart rate monitor works great. Calorie burn is close. I love the alarm when it works, which is not consistent. Online help is not helpful. I can't get the Pandora to sinc with the watch, which is one of the reasons I purchased it. Many times the screen gets "stuck". You can swipe and swipe and the screen won't move. Again, online help is NOT helpful. It looks good. The battery life is great. Thankfully it comes with a longer band if you have a larger wrist. It is fine for basic stats, but fancier stuff isn't worth the money,

I waited a long time and did a lot of research to find a smart watch to fit in my Android dominated life, with minimal bloatware, etc. This was a gift to myself (and a small compromise) for a big promotion. I'm mostly happy with it, but the battery life is disappointing to say the least. I bought the Fitbit Versa 3 new in Nov 2021 and was able to go a full week before charging it for a few months. Then five days. Then four days. Now three days, and it's June 1, 2022... I guess I'll be getting the Pixel Smart Watch earlier than I planned to. Very sad, disappointed, and really upset that I splurged and compromised, and I'm not sure it will last me a year. SO WASTEFUL! Grrr....

The tracker is A+! The band irritated my wrist so badly that I applied liquid bandage for 2 days to clear it up.  I have never had latex/silicone allergies! Some have reported allergic reaction to the metal contacts on the tracker. I did NOT have this reaction.  Replacement band from different manufacturer is working well, no reaction.

The first watch we got would register 1-3K steps./day sitting on the counter. We did not contact fitbit directly (had this problem a few years ago with a different watch and -- warning -- they replaced it with a "new" watch which was actually reconditioned) so we've returned it.  On the plus side, setup and connecting the watch to the cellphone ... they've improved that experience.  But while trying to figure it out... at first blush, I gotta say that the menus are kinda jenky... not well thought out and a few menu items lead to dead ends. Plus... they advertise it can store music, but a couple of the other reviews say you have to purchase the service to get a feature you paid for on the watch to work. Cheezy.

Overall decent, but have not had a great experience with this Versa compared to previous versions. The day of the week and time often stall and I need to let my battery deplete in order to reset. I've also had to uninstall/reinstall the app several times. Hoping it's just mine, but wanted to share.

I had a Fitbit years ago and loved it. These newer versions are just like newer versions of computer software, most times are not better and certainly not more user friendly. I really am not very happy with this Versa 3, and the battery life is ridiculously short. I wouldn't recommend it.

I have had this Versa 3 for 2 weeks. This morning it turned off and won't turn back on. I contacted customer service and worked through the trouble shooting process. They were very helpful but it still wont turn on. They are starting the return process. I'm angry! I researched all sport watches and settled on the Versa 3. $200.00 and 2 weeks later it doesn't work.  I recieved a new one within a week from Amazon. I am hoping that this one is not defective. I also bought the 2 year protection plan. With the first one dying so quickly, I am going to make sure I am covered if this one goes also.

i purchased this watch 1/2023... it is now 3/24 and it does not hold a charge... therefore I am having to put out more money and buy a new one... disappointed because I have been with fit bit brand for years... i am going with garmin this time... :(
I bought this to track my swimming. There is a glitch where it stays in swim mode and you can't get it out. Also, the one side has the band falling off often. Other than that, it is fine.

The screen has gone black after a year of normal usage. There doesn't seem to be any fix online that works, and this is a common issue with this model. The screen needs a replacement, but it is no longer under warranty.  I would invest your money elsewhere if you are looking to purchase.  Otherwise, the watch worked fine before the screen went black.

Suddenly stopped working. Fitbit is unable to help since it wasn’t purchased through them or a partner manufacturer. Definitely something to consider if you are thinking of buying a Fitbit. I also couldn’t find a way to contact the seller.

Band gave my wrist a rash, but I’m allergic to latex & silicone. Biggest complaint is that it stopped working less than 10 months of using… Took it off to shower & did not use it every day either. No warranty protection. Not worth $150+ spent

This is my second Versa. I replaced my Versa 2 with the 3. On the plus side, the heart rate monitor is much much accurate than on the previous model. However, the negatives outweigh the positives. The most frustrating thing is the call and text message notifications. I consistently received them with the Versa 2. On the 3, I am REPEATEDLY (meaning AT LEAST daily) doing a reset to get my notifications. Also, the floor counting is wacky. Today it says I've climbed 10 floors. In reality, I walked a couple of miles on a flat treadmill and my home has no stairs. Fitbit could and should be doing much better than this.

I've been Team Fitbit for a long time. I lost my last one which I had for years &it still worked great. I decided to upgrade to the Versa 3 given the great history I've had with the device. It's pretty equivalent to my previous fitbits with 1 notable exception, the battery life sucks on this version! My last fitbit went 4-5 days before needing a charge- with much older technology. I'm lucky to get a day &half out of this 1. I can't really comment on the sleep tracker b/c often times I'm not wearing it to bed since I have to place it on the charger at night. The other features are pretty decent though.

I loved the watch but am tired of the m only lasting approx. a year. I bought my Versa 3 Sept 20, 2022. It died September 4, 2023. My Versa 2 did about the same and the 2 before that. I plan on buying a different brand from now on. Disappointed in Fitbit.
